description: Import Gacs-style thickness as a structural quality functional for partial certificates. Instead of claiming the Kakeya forcing system is a Toom rule, use thickness gain as a pruning statistic that filters motifs before exact linear-algebra extraction.
mathematical_formalization: Define a thickness surrogate \Theta(A,T) on partially solved sets A\subseteq V by penalizing narrow bottlenecks and disconnected active shells. Prefer candidate local rules with \Theta(A_{t+1},T_t)-\Theta(A_t,T_t) \ge \delta>0 for most reachable states, then verify whether large \Theta correlates with low extracted score S.
analogical_connections: Toom thickness is repurposed as a geometric regularizer for arithmetic proof fronts.
Consensus-forming CA become a heuristic for eliminating thin, fragile certificate geometries.
The target direction (1,-1) acts like a preferred orientation inside an anisotropic majority dynamics.
implementation_hypothesis: Define thickness on the support of relation candidates that can already produce a target-direction singleton after local elimination. Use it as a branch-and-bound score while enumerating CA motifs and discard branches whose thickness stagnates.
experiment_seed: For every motif accepted by the droplet compiler on grids up to 8x8, compute the rank correlation between thickness gain and true extracted score. If the correlation is weak after controlling for edge density and seed count, abandon the heuristic.

closest_prior_art.title: A Toom rule that increases the thickness of sets
Universality for two-dimensional critical cellular automata
Sum-difference exponents for boundedly many slopes, and rational complexity

novelty_claim: The novelty is not a new Toom-type theorem. It is the use of a thickness-like invariant as an explicit pruning functional for exact arithmetic certificate search.
differentiation: No prior paper above optimizes or even defines arithmetic Kakeya score through a thickness surrogate. If the surrogate fails empirically, the concept should be dropped rather than inflated into a broader CA claim.
